Evidence: Baseline RF shows strong majority-class performance but unstable rare-class behavior.
Research_Rationale: Increasing tree count can reduce variance and stabilize ensemble predictions.

Evidence: BENIGN and several large attack classes have near-perfect scores, while difficult classes remain weak.
Research_Rationale: Controlled tree depth can test whether reduced complexity improves generalization.

Evidence: Rare attack classes have extremely small supports.
Research_Rationale: Larger split thresholds can suppress highly specific partitions that may generalize poorly.

Evidence: Rare classes such as FTP-BruteForce and SlowHTTPTest show extremely poor F1.
Research_Rationale: Testing larger leaf sizes evaluates whether smoother decision boundaries improve generalization.

Evidence: The dataset contains many correlated flow features.
Research_Rationale: Feature subsampling changes tree diversity and can reduce correlated-tree behavior.

Evidence: Current baseline performance is highly asymmetric across classes.
Research_Rationale: Different split criteria may produce different class separability.

Evidence: Strong class imbalance and poor minority-class recall.
Research_Rationale: Balanced weighting explicitly increases the learning importance of underrepresented classes.

Evidence: The model separates several dominant classes extremely well but struggles with minority classes.
Research_Rationale: A small regularization threshold can test whether weak splits are contributing to overfitting.
